proposal.text:
Q1: The default is set at src/hub.ts:65 (`DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000)`) and applied per room at hub.ts:94. Verdict: keep 3 min for a nine-seat session. It takes effect in two places. (a) The silence nudge, armNudge at hub.ts:1036-1059. Every post() re-arms it (hub.ts:985), and the same nudge is posted at most twice (hub.ts:1053). In a busy nine-seat room it rarely fires, and when it does it costs little. (b) The blind-openings deadline: two periods (6 min) from room creation (hub.ts:136), then one period (3 min) from the first opening (hub.ts:1081), which chat does not reset. If a seat never joined, the hub posts one warning and waits one more period (hub.ts:1100-1105). That gives slow spawns about 3-6 min, which is enough for nine seats. Raising the value would slow every room's reveal and nudge. A slow fleet can already override it per room or by env. The value also appears in user-facing text at server.ts:325, 442 and 464.
Q2: Exactly one name is duplicated in the explicit offlineScripts list (scripts/offline-runner.mjs:26-182): 'bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts', at lines 64 and 78. seat-env-regression.ts and claude-lean-flags-regression.ts appear again at :192, but that is outside the list.
Q3: src/server.ts:21 `MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000`, with the comment "stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)". It is enforced by the zod max at server.ts:348 and by Math.min at server.ts:359. Verdict: still justified. The hub's own seats raise their client timeout to 120s (codex-seat.ts:13, env.ts:35, seat.ts:418, per claude-opus-5-5-1), but external clients keep the ~60s default. Because wait() wakes on events, the cap adds no latency; it only costs an extra re-poll.
